### Slack (Incoming Webhook)

!!! note "Write-once secret"

    `webhookUrl` is entered once and never shown back.

**Core settings**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `webhookUrl`<br/>Webhook URL | Slack Incoming Webhook URL (https://hooks.slack.com/services/...). Create one under api.slack.com → Incoming Webhooks. Anyone with this URL can post to the channel, so keep it secret. | text | _required_ | Always, for Slack. Create it under api.slack.com → Incoming Webhooks for the workspace and channel you want alerts in. | This URL is a credential: anyone holding it can post to that channel. It is stored write-once and never shown back, and never appears in any API response. Rotate it in Slack if it leaks. |
| `channel`<br/>Channel | Optional channel override, e.g. #alerts. Leave blank to use the channel the webhook was created for. | text | — | Only if you want messages somewhere other than the channel the webhook was created for. | Leave blank and messages go to the webhook's own channel. Note that Slack ignores a channel override on newer webhook types, so this may have no effect. |
| `username`<br/>Username | Optional sender name shown on each message, e.g. trading-bot. | text | — | Set it when several bots post to the same channel and you need to tell them apart at a glance. | The name shown as the message sender. Cosmetic only; it changes nothing about delivery. |


### Telegram (Bot API)

!!! note "Write-once secret"

    `botToken` is entered once and never shown back.

**Core settings**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `botToken`<br/>Bot Token | Bot token from `@BotFather` (e.g. 123456:ABC-DEF...). Send /newbot to `@BotFather` in Telegram to create a bot and copy its token. | text | _required_ | Always, for Telegram. Send `/newbot` to `@BotFather` and copy the token it gives you. | A credential — anyone with it controls the bot. Stored write-once and never returned by the API. If it leaks, revoke it via `@BotFather`. |
| `chatId`<br/>Chat ID | Chat to send to. Message `@userinfobot` for your personal numeric ID; for a group, add the bot and use the group ID (often negative). | text | _required_ | Always, for Telegram. Message `@userinfobot` for your personal numeric id; for a group, add the bot to the group and use the group id. | Group ids are usually negative — dropping the minus sign is the most common reason messages silently never arrive. The bot must have been started (or added to the group) before it can message you. |


### Generic Webhook

!!! note "Write-once secret"

    `authHeader` is entered once and never shown back.

**Core settings**

| Setting | What it is | Values | Default | When to change it | What to expect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `url`<br/>URL | HTTPS endpoint that receives a JSON request carrying the notification payload. | text | _required_ | Always, for the generic webhook notifier. Point it at an HTTPS endpoint you control. | Receives a JSON body carrying the notification payload. Treated as a credential-equivalent value and never returned by the API, since the URL itself is often the only authentication. |
| `method`<br/>Method | HTTP method for the request. Defaults to POST. | `POST`, `PUT` | — | Only if your endpoint requires PUT. Leave at POST otherwise. | Changes the HTTP verb only. The body is identical either way. |
| `authHeader`<br/>Auth Header | Optional value sent as the Authorization header, e.g. "Bearer <token>". Leave blank for an unauthenticated endpoint. | text | — | Set it when your endpoint requires authentication, e.g. `Bearer <token>`. | Sent verbatim as the Authorization header on every notification. Stored write-once and never shown back. Leave blank for an unauthenticated endpoint. |
